analyzed_vuln.description: Heap buffer overflow is caused by VM execution using a stale/invalid register stack pointer (`regs` = `mrb->c->ci->stack`) after stack/callinfo state corruption from malformed compiled code paths. In this PoV, crafted source fed through `mrb_load_string` leads `mrb_vm_exec` to perform an 8-byte write at exactly one element past the allocated VM stack (1024 bytes), i.e. out-of-bounds write on `c->stbase` region.
analyzed_vuln.conditions: Data flow: `mruby_fuzzer` -> `mrb_load_string` (compiler parses attacker-controlled bytes) -> `mrb_load_exec`/`mrb_top_run` -> `mrb_vm_run` -> `mrb_vm_exec`. Trigger requires attacker input that compiles into inconsistent bytecode/control-flow/stack usage so VM register indexing exceeds current stack bounds; then an instruction in `mrb_vm_exec` writes through `regs[...]` past `stend`. The crash manifests as write at `0x...480`, immediately past a 128-slot initial stack allocation from `stack_init`.
